items.title: At least 1 dead, 6 injured after under-construction building collapses near Karachi's Baloch Colony
items.description:
KARACHI: At least one person was killed and six were injured on Wednesday after a six-storey under construction building collapsed near Karachi’s Baloch Colony, as rescue teams continued searching the rubble for people feared trapped.
A Rescue 1122 spokesperson said teams have recovered one body and rescued one person alive from the rubble. An urban search and rescue team is present at the site, the spokesperson added.
At least six injured individuals were shifted to the Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre (JPMC), the Edhi Foundation said, adding that its teams continued operations at the site.

items.description:

A meeting, presided over by the premier, was held to review the NCCIA’s performance, administrative structure and future strategy.

items.title: ‘A new era begins’: Pakistan’s Zeeshan Ali enters new frontier as Shenzhou-24 docks with space station
items.description:
China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft, carrying 40-year-old Pakistani astronaut Zeeshan Ali, successfully docked with the Tiangong space station three hours and 38 minutes after liftoff, the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) confirmed on Wednesday.
    
        
    
        
    

        
    
Ali became the first Pakistani astronaut to enter orbit after the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft successfully reached its preset orbit following liftoff from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre earlier today. And he is also the first foreign national to board the Tiangong space station.

items.title: Pakistan calls for human control over decisions on nuclear weapons use
items.description:
UNITED NATIONS: Pakistan has called for keeping decisions on the use of nuclear weapons under human control and warned that artificial intelligence (AI) systems must never be used to target nuclear command, control and communications systems.
The warning was delivered by Pakistan’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Syed Haider Shah, during a high-level open debate of the UN Security Council on Wednesday on conflict resolution in an era of rapid technological change.

items.title: Cashless divide
items.description:
IMAGINE a woman in Islamabad arriving at a government office to pay a fee. She has the money, but no bank account and no smartphone of her own. The counter no longer accepts cash. The official points her towards a QR code. She asks someone nearby to make the payment for her. The payment goes through, but she has had to depend on a stranger to make it.

items.description:

items.title: Free speech not a licence to cross four red lines: Naqvi
items.description:
• Says social media platforms acted on just 47pc of CTD complaints• Urges them to act against terrorist groups operating on their networks
ISLAMABAD: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Tuesday asserted that freedom of speech should not become a shield for those who cross “red lines”, asserting that terrorism, hate speech, incitement to violence and sexual exploitation of children were the four non-negotiable red lines for the state.
He made these remarks while addressing a seminar, Social Media Platforms and the Post-Truth Era, organised by the Sustainable Deve­lopment Policy Institute (SDPI).

items.title: India stops ‘cockroach’ drive leader from flying to London
items.description:
NEW DELHI: A leader of India’s youth-led “Cockroach” movement has said he was prevented from leaving New Delhi to fly to Britain to deliver talks on the viral group’s protests.
Saurav Das, 27, has been at the forefront of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), which has amassed millions of social media followers since its launch in May.
Das, who was due to fly out early Tuesday, said immigration officials told him at the airport that his passport had been flagged.
The incident comes a month after he was detained for defying a security crackdown in New Delhi during protests demanding the resignation
